channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Obtaining a Medical Degree in Kazakhstan to Become More Challenging
item.description: Kazakhstan has updated its medical and pharmaceutical education programs, introducing mandatory independent knowledge and skills assessments after the third year for integrated medical students. Failing this evaluation will result in academic debt and potential expulsion, making graduation more difficult.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Restrictions on Fast Food and Sugary Drinks in Educational Institutions
item.description: Kazakh lawmakers are proposing amendments to limit fast food advertising and sales in organizations for children, including colleges. This initiative aims to address rising rates of childhood obesity and type 2 diabetes in Kazakhstan. The proposed measures focus on restricting aggressive promotion and accessibility of unhealthy products in educational settings.

item.title: Moscow to Increase Migrant Work Permit Fees Starting 2027
item.description: Moscow plans to raise the monthly cost of work permits for foreign laborers starting in 2027. Fees will increase to 11,000 rubles for those employed by organizations or individual entrepreneurs, and 15,600 rubles for those working for private individuals. The proposed increase is linked to rising average wages in sectors typically employing migrant workers.

item.title: Uzbek Medical Staff May Be Employed in Hungary, Officials Discuss Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan's ambassador met with Hungary's parliamentary state secretary to discuss healthcare cooperation. Hungary expressed interest in employing Uzbek nurses and mid-level medical personnel. Both sides agreed to exchange information on placing Uzbek medical staff in European countries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Railway Sector Achieves Progress with New Lines and International Projects
item.description: In the last five years, Kyrgyzstan has launched a new railway line and begun construction on a major international project. "Kyrgyz Temir Zholu" reported increased freight volume, improved passenger services, and better social conditions for employees. The Balychy-Kochkor line is operational, and construction on the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is underway.

item.title: Kazakh MP Criticizes Ministries, Samruk-Kazyna, and Baiterek for Economic Discrepancies
item.description: Member of Parliament Daniya Yespayeva has criticized several ministries, Samruk-Kazyna, and Baiterek for a significant gap between official economic reports and the country's reality. She highlighted that despite positive macroeconomic statistics, a deep institutional disconnect persists, with departments focusing on narrow indicators rather than systemic synergy.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Pilot Project for Loans Backed by Digital Assets
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a pilot project to offer loans backed by various digital assets, as outlined in a document by the National Bank. Decentralized finance (DeFi) allows automatic exchange of digital assets, provision of loans, and other financial services without intermediaries, utilizing blockchain and smart contracts.

item.title: International Fugitive Arrested in Turkey and Extradited to Uzbekistan for Fraud
item.description: An individual wanted internationally for fraud has been apprehended in Turkey and extradited to Uzbekistan following joint operational efforts by the interior ministries of both countries. The suspect is accused of defrauding citizens of significant assets. Cooperation between law enforcement agencies continues to locate other fugitives.

item.title: Rethinking Afghanistan's Security Beyond the Absence of War
item.description: This article examines Afghanistan's security situation post-Taliban takeover, questioning the Taliban's definition of security as merely the absence of war. It argues that contemporary security studies encompass military, political, economic, societal, and environmental dimensions, moving beyond a purely military framework.

item.title: Afghanistan's Annual Inflation Reaches 7.8% Amid Rising Food Prices
item.description: Afghanistan's annual inflation rate hit 7.8% in September 2026, with food prices increasing by 8.9% year-on-year, according to the World Food Program. Rising costs for food, housing, healthcare, and transportation are pressuring households already facing unemployment and low wages.

item.title: Two Uzbek Citizens Die in Fire Incident in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A fire at a construction site in Kyrgyzstan has resulted in the deaths of two Uzbek citizens. Four Uzbek workers were present at the site when the fire broke out. One of the victims is reported to be in a coma.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports 18.4% Decrease in Theft Incidents This Year
item.description: The number of theft crimes in Kazakhstan has decreased by 18.4% in the first 10 months of this year. Apartment burglaries dropped by 23.3%, and livestock theft by 6.7%. Over 9,000 individuals were apprehended, and the activities of 1,248 criminal groups were disrupted.

item.title: Over 5,400 Bishkek Subscribers to Face Power Outages Due to Debt
item.description: More than 5,400 subscribers in Bishkek are scheduled for remote power disconnection on November 24 due to outstanding electricity bills. The Bishkek Electric Networks enterprise will use intelligent meters for automatic disconnections. Residents are urged to pay their debts promptly to avoid service interruption. Information on account balances and payment options is available online and via mobile app.

item.title: 1.1 Billion Tenge in Agricultural Subsidies Embezzled in Turkistan Region
item.description: Authorities in Turkistan have uncovered a scheme where 1.1 billion tenge allocated for agricultural machinery subsidies was embezzled. The suspect allegedly organized the illegal acquisition of state support funds intended for purchasing rain irrigation machines. Investigations revealed that 37 out of 81 machines were never delivered, despite falsified acceptance documents, leading to significant state losses.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Attract $1.3 Billion from Islamic Development Bank for SEZs
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to attract $1.3 billion from the Islamic Development Bank to develop infrastructure for its Special Economic Zones (SEZs). The funds will be used for engineering and production infrastructure, which must be ready before investors arrive. A new SEZ model is being developed, including transferring management to investors and assessing projects to avoid overcapacity.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Allocates Additional 271 Million Som for Livestock Breeding Support
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has allocated an additional 271 million som for preferential lending to support pedigree livestock breeding. Farmers can access these funds at 3% annual interest until the end of 2026. The Ministry of Agriculture reported that this funding aims to facilitate the acquisition of high-quality breeding stock.

item.title: Kazakhstan Mandates Justification for Repeated Redirection of Citizen Appeals
item.description: Kazakh government bodies are now required to provide written justifications for repeatedly redirecting citizen appeals between agencies. This new rule, effective November 8th, aims to address growing complaints about formal responses and excessive inter-agency transfers. Appeals redirected more than three times must be explained.

item.title: Turkestan Region Investigates Over 1 Billion Tenge Subsidy Theft
item.description: The Turkestan Region's Agency for Financial Monitoring is investigating the alleged embezzlement of over 1 billion tenge in budget funds. These funds were allocated for subsidizing the purchase of agricultural equipment, with 37 irrigation machines reportedly not delivered.

item.title: Central Bank Employees in Afghanistan Face Death Threats Under Taliban Rule
item.description: Sources report that employees of a Da Afghanistan Bank branch, under Taliban control, have received death threats for three weeks. Some employees who worked under the former government are being followed and warned. One employee, Najib, was reportedly killed on November 13. The Taliban-controlled bank is aware but has taken no serious action.

item.title: Taliban Health Ministry to Suspend Hospitals Failing Accreditation Standards
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Public Health announced it will suspend hospitals that do not meet accreditation standards. Minister Noor Jalal Jalali stated that hospitals failing to meet requirements will be given a short period to rectify deficiencies. If issues persist, their operations will be halted. This follows a recent assessment in Kabul where 115 private hospitals were categorized.

item.title: Russian Interpol Requests Lead Central Asia's Presence on International Wanted Lists
item.description: Russia leads the world in Interpol requests, with its databases accessible to CIS police. A new guide helps Kyrgyz citizens understand and challenge international wanted status. Many Kyrgyz citizens working or traveling abroad discover they are wanted only at border control. The guide highlights that while Interpol prohibits political cases, disputes can be disguised as criminal charges.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Tax Exemption for Bank Debt Forgiveness
item.description: A proposal in Kazakhstan suggests exempting individuals from personal income tax on debt forgiven by banks and microfinance organizations. This aims to alleviate tax burdens for citizens unable to repay loans. Additionally, limits on the amount of debt financial institutions can write off are being considered, potentially reducing the write-off limit from 10% to 5% for banks.

item.title: Uzbekistan Begins Talks with Australia on Labor Migration Opportunities
item.description: Uzbekistan has initiated discussions with the regional government of Australia's Northern Territory regarding organized labor migration. Representatives from Uzbekistan's Migration Agency and Ministry of Foreign Affairs held online negotiations. The talks focused on Australia's demand for skilled workers, particularly in the oil and gas sector, and mechanisms for legal employment and training of Uzbek specialists.

item.title: Bishkek Strengthens Embankments of Big Chuy Canal Section
item.description: Bishkek is undertaking embankment reinforcement work on an 800-meter section of the Big Chuy Canal, between Orozbekov and Abdrakhmanov streets. Gabion structures are being installed on both sides to prevent further erosion. The project also includes landscaping, a road asphalt overlay, and the creation of a public recreational space along the canal.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Implement Digital Control Over Construction Materials in 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to introduce digital control over construction materials in 2027, designated as the Year of National Construction. This initiative aims to monitor the use of domestic and imported materials from project design to completion. The Ministry of Industry and Construction stated that this will ensure domestic materials are used and prevent unjustified substitutions.

item.title: Flash Floods and Mudflows Possible in Mountainous Areas of Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzhydromet has warned of possible flash floods and mudflows in the mountainous and foothill regions of Uzbekistan on November 24 due to expected rainfall. The Tashkent region's Angren, Bostanlyk, Parkent, Pskent, Urta Chirchik, and Yukori Chirchik districts, along with the cities of Angren and Almalyk, are particularly affected. Residents are advised to take precautions.

item.title: Over 16,000 Central Asians Arrive in Novosibirsk for Work, While Net Migration Declines
item.description: Novosibirsk Oblast has seen 16,052 residents from Central Asia arrive for work since early November. However, the region's net migration has turned negative, with 25,888 migrants departing. Over 2,000 illegal migrants were expelled for violating immigration laws. Authorities are conducting checks on various sites to enforce regulations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Registers Property Rights for Over 1.3 Million Real Estate Objects
item.description: Uzbekistan's Cadastre Agency has registered property rights for 1,328,234 real estate objects, issuing 885,671 cadastral passports. Electronic maps of 42.4 million hectares of land have been created. Over 8 million archival documents have been digitized, and over 35,000 land plots have been put up for auction.

item.title: Avalanche Prevention Measures Underway at 'Ala-Too Resort' Mountain Cluster
item.description: Preparations are being made to organize and improve the work of the avalanche safety station at the 'Ala-Too Resort' mountain cluster. Specialists are training station staff for the cluster's official opening on December 1. The station's primary role is to monitor avalanche risks and coordinate preventative actions in the area.

item.title: Kazakhstan banks seek greater freedom for business lending
item.description: Banks in Kazakhstan are seeking to have their hands untied to facilitate lending to businesses. The specific measures or regulatory changes desired are not detailed in the provided text, but the aim is to boost corporate financing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes mandatory QR-code labeling for halal products
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering mandatory QR-code labeling for halal products and services, along with creating four market participant registries. The proposed amendments to the law on the halal industry require a compliance certificate and special marking, including a national 'halal' mark with a unique QR code.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Defense Lawyers Withdraw from Sanjar Bokaev Trial Over Judge Dispute
item.description: Defense lawyers in the Sanjar Bokaev case have withdrawn from a court session after the judge repeatedly denied their recusal requests. The prosecution had asked to exclude testimony from a key witness, citing concerns about his impartiality. The judge supported the prosecution's motion, leading the defense to declare they would not continue participating in the proceedings.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Over 9,000 Arrests for Theft in 10 Months, Crime Groups Dismantled
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs reported a 18.4% decrease in overall thefts and a 23.3% drop in burglaries during the first 10 months of the year. Over 9,000 individuals were detained, and 1,248 criminal groups were neutralized. The ministry highlighted successful operations in Taraz and Turkestan region, recovering stolen valuables.

item.title: Kazakhstan Eases Debt Restructuring for Borrowers Facing Difficulties
item.description: Kazakhstan is simplifying debt restructuring for citizens struggling to repay loans from multiple banks or microfinance organizations. Borrowers can now negotiate a unified payment schedule with a single application, avoiding separate requests to each creditor. Options include reducing monthly payments, extending loan terms, or deferring payments.

item.title: Analysts Warn of Potential AI-95 Gasoline Shortage in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Analysts warn of potential risks to gasoline supply in Kyrgyzstan due to unplanned repairs at Russian refineries following drone attacks. While current reserves may prevent immediate shortages, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan remain vulnerable due to high import reliance. Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan mitigate risks with domestic refining capacity.

item.title: Three Police Officers Injured in Knife Attack in Mashhad, Iran
item.description: Three police officers were injured in Mashhad, Iran, after an attack by two individuals wielding knives. One attacker was killed during the incident, according to local police. Psychotropic pills were reportedly found among the suspects' belongings. Investigations into the motive are ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports 9.3% Industrial Production Growth, Highest in 25 Years
item.description: Kazakhstan's industrial production grew by 9.3% in the first ten months of 2026, marking the highest rate in 25 years. The Minister of Industry and Construction, Ersain Nagaspayev, stated that manufacturing output has increased by 14.5% over the past three years, with investments doubling to 3 trillion tenge. Metallurgy accounts for approximately 40% of the manufacturing sector, employing around 109,000 people.

item.title: UN: 5.5 Million People in Afghanistan Gained Access to Water Through 'Abadi' Project
item.description: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) reports that 5.5 million people in Afghanistan, including 2.7 million women and girls, have gained access to water through the 'Abadi' project between January 2022 and September 2026. The UNDP stated that access to water transforms lives in Afghanistan. A World Bank report indicated only 31% of the population had access to safe drinking water by 2024.

item.title: US Questions Streamer Sneako After Afghanistan Trip, Seizes Electronic Devices
item.description: US authorities questioned American streamer Sneako for eight hours and seized his electronic devices after his return from Afghanistan, where he met with Taliban officials. Sneako stated he was questioned at Abu Dhabi airport and upon arrival in New York, with his phone and other devices confiscated. The questioning followed his controversial visit to Afghanistan.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host Third Tajikistan International Mining and Metallurgy Forum on Critical Minerals
item.description: The third Tajikistan International Mining and Metallurgy Forum will convene in Dushanbe on November 26, focusing on critical minerals and rare earth elements. Prime Minister Kohir Rasulzoda will open the event, which includes sessions on Tajikistan's investment climate, mining potential, and sustainable development. Memoranda of understanding are expected to be signed.
